title: Enterprise reservation qualification & dynamic scaling guidance
creator: Priya Nair
description: Objective: Create a concise qualification and scaling guidance artifact that enables Sales/SEs and Solutions to consistently map enterprise customer needs to reservation tiers, GPU family recommendations, SLA targets, and autoscale policies. This ticket captures the rubric, an example decision matrix, onboarding checklist, and one-page cheat sheet for pre-sales conversations. Scope excludes implementation of autoscaling code paths; we are delivering prescriptive guidance and intake artifacts for the onboarding workflow.
acceptance_criteria: A clear qualification rubric that maps customer signals (RPS, 95th/99th latency targets, model family, concurrency, QPS burst profile, and data residency) to one of five reservation tiers.
A decision matrix that recommends GPU class (A100-80GB, A10G, H100e, or c5+CPU-only fallback) based on model type (LLamaX/gpt-style), token length distribution, and cost sensitivity.
Autoscale policy templates (min/max nodes, burst buffer, pre-warming rules) for each reservation tier and expected workload pattern.
An intake checklist and sample filled form for Solutions to use during customer discovery calls.
A single-page cheat sheet PDF for Sales summarizing SLA/throughput tradeoffs and negotiation levers.
Document links and handoff notes posted to Confluence and referenced in the onboarding playbook.
decision_log: 2026-02-28: Kickoff—aligned on goal to reduce manual sizing variance between SEs. Owner: Priya Nair.
2026-03-01: Chose to standardize on 5 reservation tiers instead of free-form sizing to simplify contracting (agreed: Small/Medium/Large/X-Large/Custom). Reviewer: Alex Rodriguez (Sales Eng).

2026-03-03: For latency-sensitive models (<200ms 95th), recommend H100e or A100-80GB depending on batchability; for throughput-bound but cost-sensitive, recommend A10G or mixed CPU fallback. Infra input: Lars Becker.
2026-03-05: Autoscale approach finalized—use conservative min nodes + burst buffer + pre-warm window; will hand implementation to ENG after documentation is approved.
triage_notes: Primary signals used in rubric: sustained request rate (RPS), expected concurrency, token generation per request (median & 95th), model family & quantization profile, required geo/region, and uptime SLO.
Tradeoff: aggressive autoscaling reduces cost but increases cold-start latency risk; playbook favors SLA preservation over aggressive cost saving for enterprise tier.
Edge cases: Customers with extreme burst patterns (spikes >10x sustained) should be routed to 'Custom' tier and include dedicated burst pool with contractual pre-warm triggers.
We avoid tight GPU family guarantees for hosted tier; instead we provide recommended families and a fallback plan documented in the SLA appendix.
customer_examples: Case A - Conversational commerce startup: Needs 50 RPS steady, 95th latency <350ms, median token length 64. Recommendation: Medium reservation tier on A100-80GB with KV cache enabled and min_nodes=2, max_nodes=6, burst buffer=30%.

Case B - Enterprise search + reranking: Burst-driven (sustained 5 RPS, peaks to 200 RPS during business hours), cost sensitive, model is quantized open model. Recommendation: Large reservation on A10G with aggressive batching, pre-warm scheduled nodes for morning peak, set burst buffer=60% and max_nodes to cap cost.

Case C - Regulated on-prem migration: Requires VPC/on-prem control, expected throughput low (1-2 RPS) but strict 99.9% uptime and audit logs. Recommendation: Small reservation with private deployment + service-level fallback to dedicated pool for critical windows; include on-call escalation playbook.
